title: CRLR/126/2023 of PANKAJ SHARMA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY HOME DEHRADUN

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 126 of 2023
Pankaj Sharma ....Revisionist
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand and Others ..... Respondents
Mr. Vivek Kumar, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. J.S. Virk, D.A.G.. for the State of Uttarakhand.

JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 The challenge in this revision is made to
the order of interim maintenance dated 07.02.2023,
passed in Case No. 13 of 2022, Smt. Indu Lata Sharma
and Shri Pankaj Sharma, by the court of Family Judge,
Haridwar ("the case"). By it, the interim maintenance
application, filed by the private respondents has been
allowed and the revisionist has been directed to pay Rs.
6,000/- per month as interim maintenance to the
respondent no.2, Smt. Indu Lata Sharma, his wife, and
Rs. 7,000/- to each of the respondent nos. 2 and 3, Km.
Satakshi Vats and Km. Vaniya, respectively, as interim
maintenance.
2. Heard learned counsel for the revisionist
and perused the record.

2
3. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that the salary of the revisionist is Rs. 59,000/-
per month. His wife, the respondent no.2, is also
working and gets about Rs. 12,000/- per month salary.
Therefore, the amount, as interim maintenance, to the
respondent no.2 is on higher side.
4. If a wife is earning, merely because of this
fact, she is not disentitled to maintenance or interim
maintenance. Maintenance or interim maintenance is
awarded keeping in view the income of the parties and
their social status. Two children of the revisionist are
staying with his wife, i.e. the respondent no.2. If income
of both the revisionist and his wife, the respondent no.2,
is added, it comes around Rs. 70,000/- and by virtue of
the interim order, the respondent no.2 gets total Rs.
32,000/- to maintain herself and her two children, i.e.
respondent nos. 3 and 4, and the revisionist is left with
Rs. 38,000.
5. A wife and children are definitely entitled to
get maintenance commensurate with the income and
social status of the husband. That is what has been
done by the impugned order. Therefore, this Court does
not see any reason to make any interference in this

3
revision. Accordingly, the revision deserves to be
dismissed, at the stage of admission itself.
6. The revision is dismissed in limine.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 24.02.2023
